newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia overnight rises high despite maturity.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia overnight rises high despite maturity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to 8.30/60 percent against 8.00/40 percent as demand for funds remained high despite the maturity of a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said on Friday.
"There is no apparent reason for the overnight to be so high because the market is quite liquid and there is also a maturity," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said the market was widely expecting a decline in interbank rates after the maturity neutralised a mismatch in funds flow since Wednesday.
Banks on Wednesday had paid out one billion ringgit for two Bank Negara bill issues against a maturity of 500 million.
"One reason could be that people have begun withdrawing cash for the festival season because new currency notes have come into the market," said the head of money dealing at another bank.
Earlier, other interbank rates were mostly unchanged as the market remained liquid.
Dealers said the market was cautious, wondering why interest rates were not falling despite a sharp rise in liquidity on the back of a strengthening ringgit.
The ringgit has gained around two percent against the U.S. dollar in the last 10 days.
One-week money was at 7.10/20 percent, two-week at 7.10/20, one- and three-month at 7.25 and six-month at 7.35/38, all unchanged from their previous levels.
Dealers said the market is expected to remain flush next week and bring down interbank rates further.
